summary:
Norfolk Island, Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Jervis Bay Territory have no territory-specific law on gender identity, sexual orientation or intersex status. Each stands under Australia's national framework, which the national record carries; the territory-specific question is which body of law attaches to each.

Norfolk Island was incorporated into New South Wales legislation from 1 July 2016 under the Norfolk Island Legislation Amendment Act 2015 and the Territories Legislation Amendment Act 2016. A visitor there meets New South Wales law rather than a Norfolk Island enactment.

Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, administered together as the Australian Indian Ocean Territories, are jurisdictions in which Western Australian law applies.

Jervis Bay Territory is governed directly under Commonwealth law, and the Commonwealth Sex Discrimination Act 1984, as amended in 2013, applies throughout Australia including the external territories governed directly by Commonwealth law. That statute is the anti-discrimination framework a visitor to Jervis Bay stands under.

Availability of the 'X' sex descriptor and anti-discrimination protection on the grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity or expression extend across the states and territories alongside concurrent federal protection. No territory-specific provision on markers or on discrimination diverges from that position in the four territories.

No territory-specific rule on facilities, care access, entry or screening was located for any of the four, and no territory-specific enforcement action or incident involving a trans visitor was found.
tangentialFactors:
Because the applicable law comes from a state rather than a local enactment, the vilification and discrimination coverage a visitor meets on Norfolk Island or in the Indian Ocean Territories follows the regime of New South Wales or Western Australia respectively, not a territory provision. The same fact means a change in either state's law changes the position in the corresponding territory without any territory-level decision.

Norfolk Island's transfer to New South Wales legislation in 2016 is the only territory-level legal change documented; the Indian Ocean Territories and Jervis Bay have no comparable transfer on the sources held.
localsOnly:
For residents, the practical consequence of the framework mapping is that a discrimination or vilification complaint arising on Norfolk Island runs under New South Wales law, one arising on Christmas Island or the Cocos (Keeling) Islands under Western Australian law, and one arising in Jervis Bay Territory under Commonwealth law. No territory legislature has enacted a separate gender-identity provision.

Residents of the territories governed directly by Commonwealth law fall within the national sex discrimination statute rather than a territory enactment.
outOfScopeNotes:
No territory-specific statute, court ruling, enforcement record, care-access rule or facilities rule was located for Norfolk Island, Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands or Jervis Bay Territory. The framework mapping above rests on a single encyclopaedic source and has not been checked against the territory or state instruments themselves.

Whether the application of Western Australian law in the Indian Ocean Territories extends to the whole of that state's anti-discrimination and vilification statute, or only to part of it, is unresolved on the sources held.

No territory-level data on trans-directed violence, screening practice or entry processing was found, and nothing indicates a territory-specific risk distinct from the national position.
